title: lease-based-session-resume-and-soft-abort-protocol-v2
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce lease-based streaming session protocol (v2) with soft-abort semantics, resume tokens with last-ack sequencing, and adapter compatibility for v1 clients; opt-in via feature flag for staged rollout.
description: Motivation: reduce user-visible failures when clients disconnect during long-running streaming or function-invoke flows and avoid double-execution of tool calls while preserving backwards compatibility. This PR implements a lease-based session ownership model (session leases are short-lived ephemeral tokens that the client can present to resume an in-flight session), a server soft-abort signal that preserves KV cache and allows a short reconnect window, and a small streaming envelope version bump (v2) that separates structured-output frames from toolcall frames to make resume safe for function calls. Key changes: add X-RW-Session-Lease header and server-side lease manager with configurable TTL and jitter; introduce resume token format "lease:<id>:<last_ack_seq>:<sig>" and validation rules; implement soft-abort event code "rw:soft_abort" and a grace window during which server retains the session state; add tool-call fingerprinting to detect and suppress duplicate tool invocations on resume; extend streaming envelope with explicit frame types (emit, tool_call, tool_result, metadata) while translating v1 streams via an adapter for compatibility; expose metrics for lease failures, resume_success_rate, soft_abort_rate, and lease_refresh_latency; add unit/integration tests and e2e scenarios that simulate flaky networks and replayed resumes. Compatibility and rollout: v1 clients continue to work unchanged via the adapter that translates v2 envelope frames back to the v1 wire format; feature gated behind "session-lease-v2" (console flag + API header opt-in) so we can stage traffic 0%->20%->100% following Canary windows and perf guardrails. Security: resume tokens are HMAC-signed (KMS-backed signing key) and time-limited to avoid session hijack. Testing and verification: carried out deterministic replay tests for function call idempotency, 100x flaky reconnect capture tests, and benchmarks showing ~3% throughput improvement from lighter KV retention logic. Rollout plan: 1) enable gate in internal envs; 2) 20% user traffic for 48h with tight tracing; 3) 100% after validating resume success and low soft_abort rate. Checklist: [x] design doc linked; [x] proto and schema changes; [x] tests added; [x] docs and changelog; [x] feature-flag wiring; [x] metrics and alerts configured. Follow-ups: metrics SLO adjustments, add SDK helpers for automatic lease refresh, tighten default TTL based on real traffic patterns.
commits_summary: 5 commits: 1) session lease manager and TTL logic; 2) streaming envelope v2 frames + v1 adapter translator; 3) tool-call fingerprinting and idempotency guard; 4) tests and flaky-network e2e harness; 5) docs, feature-flag wiring, and metrics/alerts.

review_conversation: Ethan Wallace: Nice design. Two concerns: 1) lease TTL default value (30s) may be too aggressive for high-latency mobile; recommend exposing scalar in API config. 2) Please add a unit test where resume token signature fails to ensure we close session gracefully.

Maya Chen: Addressed both. TTL is now configurable via per-customer profile and the handler returns a well-defined 410:rw_lease_expired for expired tokens. Added signature-negative test in streaming_handler_test.go.

Diego Ramos: Can we be more explicit about the semantics of soft-abort vs hard-abort in the docs? I had to trace code to confirm that soft-abort keeps KV cache for 60s then transitions to hard cleanup. Request to document state transitions and alerting thresholds.
Maya Chen: Updated streaming_resilience.md with a state diagram and added metrics-based alert thresholds (soft_abort_rate > 1% fires paging alert).
Lena Park: LGT M. Verified bench numbers. Please squash and ensure migrations are reversible. Approved pending minor lint fix in session_manager.go (fixed).
